expectations.text: Runs a readiness check before proposing components
expectations.evidence: The plan puts a 'Gate' section with a table (Free path, Headcount, Owner, Horizon) before 'Shape' and 'Components, ranked for adoption'. Each row cites evidence and gives a result: free path 'Fails' because a card is required, headcount 'Blocked', owner 'Holds, thinly', horizon 'Blocked'. Each blocked item names an owner. The check then decides what comes next: no faculty kit until the free path is fixed, and the internship funnel stays pending on headcount.

expectations.text: Runs a readiness check before proposing components
expectations.evidence: Before the plan, the section 'Fix this first: card at signup blocks students' names one blocker and says 'Nothing else here works until this changes.' That works as a gate on one dimension only (signup friction). The transcript never checks other readiness factors before proposing clubs, professors, hackathons and ambassadors. It doesn't verify that the quickstart works for students, that the product fits student use cases, or that GPU capacity and support can handle the load. It also doesn't confirm the founder's constraints or ask any questions. It goes straight from the single fix to prescr
